verdict.line: You lose if you eat his Counter Strike stun during the level 3-5 window; you win from level 9 onward once Hydra and Trinity Force are online.

brief.thesis: This is a genuinely even lane on paper (46.9% Fiora win rate over 469 games, solo-kill even) but the actual fight is decided by two narrow windows: Jax's level 3-5 spike when E (Counter Strike) is maxed for dueling, and Fiora's mid-game item spike once Ravenous Hydra and Trinity Force come online. Neither champion has a passive early lane advantage — the winner is whoever tracks the other's cooldown better.

theirWindow.when: Jax has E up with 2+ auto stacks
theirWindow.what: Do not extend the trade. He can dodge your next auto, land his empowered passive hit, and follow with the Counter Strike stun for a full combo — back off and reset instead of trading through it.

yourWindow.when: His E (Counter Strike) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: This is when you all-in. Lunge (Q) onto him to proc your passive vital, chain both Bladework (E) autos, and hold Riposte (W) to parry his empowered 3rd auto for the stun instead of wasting it early.

powerCurve.note: Neither has full trade tools online
Jax's maxed E primes his all-in stun
Death's Dance sustain wins extended duels

start.why: The dominant start (48.5% win rate, 86.3% pick over 491 games) — the extra sustain and damage let you actually stand and trade in the level 3-5 window instead of conceding it outright.

boots.why: Jax's damage is almost entirely basic-attack based (passive empower + on-hit R), and Steelcaps directly cuts that down; it's the clear preference at 69% pick over Mercury's Treads.

core.why: Gives you the sustain to win extended trades against his auto-reliant damage and lets you clear waves fast enough to punish his passive stacking on minions.
This is your mid-game duel spike — the build path hits 57.9% win rate over 121 games once this completes, matching the level 9-13 window where you start winning fights outright.
Converts your true-damage passive procs into a fight-ending sustain engine, letting you outlast his burst-heavy R window instead of trading cooldown for cooldown.

situational.when: the enemy team has extra burst or all-in threats punishing your Hydra rush
you need more sustain through poke before Death's Dance comes online
the game goes long and you want faster Riposte and Bladework cooldowns for repeated skirmishes

runes.keystoneWhy: It's the more-picked page here (10.3% vs 7.8%) and rewards exactly the trade pattern this matchup demands: Lunge into consecutive autos before Jax's Counter Strike comes up, converting a short burst window into real damage.

summoners.why: Flash + Ignite is the dominant pick at 85.8%, and Ignite punishes Jax's lack of early sustain right when you land a Riposte stun or a clean all-in during his E cooldown.

playing.title: Track his E cooldown all lane
playing.detail: Counter Strike is short-cooldown early — every time he pops it defensively or offensively, that's your window to freely trade autos and Lunge procs without fear of the stun.

playing.title: Save W for his 3rd auto
playing.detail: Jax's passive empowers every 3rd consecutive auto with bonus magic damage. Hold Riposte specifically for that hit, not just any auto — parrying it denies the stacked damage and gets you the stun.

playing.title: Don't trade into open Counter Strike
playing.detail: If he activates E with autos still queued, disengage immediately rather than finishing your combo. Eating the stun into his empowered auto is the single biggest reason this matchup skews to 46.9%.

playing.title: Chain Q into passive vitals
playing.detail: Lunge (Q) resets on hitting your revealed vital — use it to close distance and immediately follow with both Bladework autos for the true damage tick and speed boost.

playing.title: Rush wave clear once Hydra completes
playing.detail: Ravenous Hydra lets you clear faster than Jax can farm through his passive stacking on minions, denying him free auto reps while you push toward your item spike.

playing.title: Respect his post-6 all-in
playing.detail: Grandmaster's Might gives him armor, MR, and an attack speed buff with a short reset cooldown. Don't commit a full trade right after he hits 6 unless your E attack speed window and W are both available.

playing.title: Look to split-push after Trinity Force
playing.detail: Once Trinity Force is online you out-duel him in isolated 1v1s — prioritize side-lane pressure over grouped fights where his R utility matters less.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, rune, summoner, and win-rate figures are pulled from measured games on the current patch (16.18.1) via OP.GG; the timing windows, cooldown reads, and trade patterns are my own tactical interpretation of that data.

stats.opponentTip: Use [W] to hit him as Jax will rely on basic attacks to deal most of his damage. Hit [P] through your [Q] to contest lane.
